lastWeekReview.title: Moses—A Prepared Person, Called By God
bullets: Baby Moses was saved from Pharaoh's order — his mother placed him in a waterproof basket on the river!
Miriam watched over her baby brother, and cleverly brought their own mother to nurse him.
God arranged for Moses to grow up in Pharaoh's palace — the best education in the world!
At age 40, Moses chose God's people over the riches of Egypt.
God led Moses to be a humble shepherd for 40 years — learning patience, humility, and compassion.
At the burning bush, God finally called Moses — fully prepared after 80 years!
lastWeekReview.discussion: 📖  What are the three things Moses needed to be prepared? (Knowledge of God, highest education, excellent character)
lastWeekReview.verseQuote: "…He will be a vessel unto honor, sanctified, useful to the master, prepared unto every good work." — 2 Timothy 2:21b

kidsContent.text: God sent Moses and his brother Aaron to Pharaoh with a clear message: "Let My people go so they can hold a feast to Me!"
But Pharaoh said "NO!" He didn't know God, and he wasn't about to let his slaves go free. Instead, he made things WORSE — he forced the Israelites to make bricks without even giving them straw!
The Israelites were so upset they blamed Moses. Moses got discouraged too! But he didn't stay discouraged — he went back to God and talked with Him.
God told Moses: "I will fulfill every promise. I am not only the promising God — I am the fulfilling God!"
So Moses had to keep going back to Pharaoh — again and again and again!
Ten Plagues — God Doesn't Give Up!
Because Pharaoh kept saying NO, God sent TEN plagues — each one worse than the last!
First came 3 bothering plagues: water turned to blood, frogs EVERYWHERE, and lice!
Then came plagues that caused real damage: swarms of flies, sickness on animals, painful boils, hail mixed with fire, locusts that ate every plant, and total darkness for three days!
After each plague, Pharaoh seemed ready to let them go — but then he hardened his heart and said "NO" again!
Moses went back to Pharaoh TWELVE times in total! Even when he felt discouraged, he went back to God and was encouraged again.
🌟 God doesn't give up — and neither should we! When friends say "no" to our invitation, don't give up. Keep inviting them, just like Moses kept going back!

image.caption: The plague of frogs covers Egypt

lesson.practicePoint: This week, think of something you've been wanting to do for God but feel discouraged about. Don't give up! Go back to God in prayer and try again. Be ready to share your story!

memoryVerse.text: …Be strong and take courage; do not be afraid or dismayed. For Jehovah your God is with you wherever you go.
memoryVerse.application: Moses felt afraid and discouraged going to Pharaoh, but God was with him every step of the way. When we feel discouraged, we can be strong and take courage because God is with us wherever we go!

parts.text: Materials: 10 numbered cards (one per plague), beanbags or soft balls, 10 cups/targets
Setup: Line up 10 cups in a row, each labeled with a plague name (1-Blood, 2-Frogs, 3-Lice, 4-Flies, 5-Livestock, 6-Boils, 7-Hail, 8-Locusts, 9-Darkness, 10-???)
Round 1: Each kid gets 3 throws to knock down cups. Even if they miss, they must try again — don't give up!
Round 2: Move the cups farther back. It's harder now! Just like it got harder for Moses each time.
Round 3: Kids must knock them down in ORDER (1 through 10). Teamwork encouraged!
After each round, ask: "Did you want to give up? Moses felt the same way — but God told him to keep going!"
📖 Connection: Moses went to Pharaoh 12 times! God doesn't give up and neither should we!

rolePlayScript.text: Scene: Pharaoh's throne room in Egypt. Pharaoh sits on his throne looking powerful.
God sent Moses and his brother Aaron to the most powerful king in the world — Pharaoh of Egypt!
Pharaoh! The God of Israel says: Let My people go, so they can hold a feast to Me!
Who is this 'God'? I don't know Him, and I will NOT let your people go! In fact — make them work HARDER! No more straw for their bricks!
The Israelites are upset. One steps forward.
Moses, this is YOUR fault! Things are worse now than before you came!
Moses felt so discouraged. But he didn't give up — he went back to God!
Lord, why have You sent me? Things are only getting worse!
I will fulfill every promise. I am not only the promising God — I am the fulfilling God! Now go back to Pharaoh!
Moses returns to Pharaoh. God sends the first plague — water turns to blood!
Pharaoh, look! God has turned all the water in Egypt to BLOOD!
Hmph! My magicians can do the same thing. The answer is still NO!
More plagues come — frogs, lice, flies! Each time Pharaoh says NO.
Fine, fine — I'll let them go! Wait... no. I changed my mind. NO!
God sent plague after plague — sickness on animals, boils, hail with fire, locusts, and total darkness! But Pharaoh hardened his heart every single time.
I've been back to Pharaoh TWELVE times! But God says don't give up — so I won't give up!
Our God doesn't give up — and neither should we! When things get hard, we go back to God and try again!

description.text: Setup: Two teams. Three stations representing plagues.
Station 1 (Frogs): Hop like a frog across the gym to the next station.
Station 2 (Darkness): Put on a blindfold and walk carefully to the next station (partner guides with voice).
Station 3 (Hail): Dodge soft balls tossed by a leader while running to the finish line.
After finishing, shout "LET MY PEOPLE GO!" Fastest team wins!
📖 Connection: Each plague was different, but God never gave up on freeing His people!
Setup: 10 spots marked around the gym, each with a plague name card.
Rules: Music plays — kids run around the gym. When music stops, a leader calls a plague number.
Kids must race to that plague's spot. Last one there does 5 jumping jacks.
Twist: After round 5, Pharaoh 'hardens his heart' — kids must do the challenge TWICE!
📖 Connection: Every time Pharaoh said NO, things got harder — but God and Moses never gave up!
Materials: 10 plague name cards, music player

movieViewing.title: The Terrible Days of Egypt
movieViewing.description: TBTMS story video — The plagues of Egypt! God sends plague after plague to convince Pharaoh to let His people go. (Exodus 5-11)

description.text: Set up an obstacle course with 10 stations — one for each plague.
Station examples: jump over cones (frogs), crawl under a rope (darkness), zigzag through markers (swarm of flies), toss a ball into a bucket (hail).
The twist: After finishing, a leader says 'Pharaoh says NO!' — and kids must run the course AGAIN!
How many times can they complete it before time runs out? (Goal: at least 3 rounds — like Moses going back!)
Materials: Cones, rope, markers, soft balls, buckets, timer

outdoor.tip: 🐸 This week covers 9 of the 10 plagues (save #10 for next week). Make sure kids understand: God wasn't being mean — He was showing His power to free His people!
